paper_metadata.title: Effect of Co on Discontinuous Precipitation Transformation with TCP Phase in Ni-based Alloy Containing Re

evidence.quote: Three experimental alloys, containing typical TCP-forming elements Re and Cr as well as different additions of Co, were investigated
Ternary alloy R0 containing 65 at. pct Ni, 25 at. pct Cr, and 10 at. pct Re is the baseline alloy.
Ternary alloy R0 containing 65 at. pct Ni, 25 at. pct Cr, and 10 at. pct Re is the baseline alloy.

Two levels of Co addition (7.0 and 15.0 at. pct) substituted for Ni were added to the baseline alloy to obtain alloys R7 and R15, respectively.

Experimental alloys were made from high purity metals in an arc melting furnace under an argon atmosphere. Each alloy button with about 20 g in weight was alternately melted 10 times in order to achieve a more homogeneous composition.
The as-cast alloy buttons were homogenized at 1593 K (1320 °C) for 8 hours

then aged at 1173 K to 1423 K (900 °C to 1150 °C) for 5 minute to 200 hours to investigate the effect of Co on microstructural evolution. All heat treatments were performed in the lab air followed by water quenching.

High-temperature heat treatment at 1593 K (1320 °C) for 8 hours eliminated the solidification segregation in the as-cast alloys and a homogeneous single gamma phase was obtained in all three alloys.
